structure: One ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-19.md, 37 lines of markdown. It is Sam's ruling given in the overview-and-review build session on 19 November 2026, answering the theme's engineering review (review:engineering-2026-11-19, https://claude.ai/artifact/TrAdrBupdoyCP4YJmXjuJL), which had listed what the theme does differently from the service's existing patterns. The file has three pieces, in order: a three-line preamble (lines 3 to 5) naming the session and the review it answers; Sam's own ruling as a numbered list of five items (lines 7 to 20), item 4 carrying a four-bullet sub-list of the exceptions that stay as they are; and a closing block headed "Orchestrator's calls applying it, which Sam accepted (\"crack on\")" (lines 22 to 37), eight bullets of applied calls, the first of which explicitly replaces the 16 November ruling's "what stays" clause on outstanding items (claim 2) and the last of which applies ruling item 2 to Delete. The two blocks carry different authority on their face — the numbered list is Sam's wording, the bullets are the orchestrator's calls that Sam accepted — and the extract must keep that distinction. The source's scope is "whole file", so nothing in it is left out; there is no other material (no attachments, no quoted review text, no code), and the review artefact it answers is a separate source, not part of this one. At 37 lines the whole file is well inside one part, and a ruling settles conflicts word by word, so it is cut as a single part.

parts.title: The whole ruling file
parts.scope: The whole of ruling-sam-2026-11-19.md, from the title on line 1 to the last bullet on line 37: the preamble, Sam's five numbered items with item 4's four exception bullets, and all eight of the orchestrator's accepted calls. Nothing is held back for another part.
covers: The preamble (lines 3 to 5): that the ruling was given in the overview-and-review build session and answers the engineering review review:engineering-2026-11-19, which listed what the theme does differently from the service's existing patterns — context for every claim, and the thing each claim's note points back to.

Numbered item 1: plants shows the notification task list heading visibly, as live animals does, with the copy "Notification task list" ("task list" as two words, the GOV.UK spelling) in both services. Claim the visibility decision and the exact copy, and that it applies to both services.

Numbered item 2: each header button gets its own form, as every other posting button in the service does — Amend, Copy as new and Delete on the notification view header, in both the live animals and plants frontends. Claim the per-button form rule, the three buttons it names and the two frontends.

Numbered item 3: tests find live animals review cards the way plants does, by GOV.UK structure and role, so no test depends on the words "2. Description of the goods"; the review page's test page object gets a single `heading` again; and the overloads that grew on the two shared helpers (resume in the UI, the save and continue walk) come out. Claim the locator rule, the page-object change and the helper-overload removal.

Numbered item 4: every other atypical item the review found is fixed — plus each of the four named exceptions as its own claim, with the reason the ruling gives: the local stack's automatic restart of the file uploader (keep); the plants journey spec ruling that was deleted rather than superseded (don't care); the tests repo's deleted docs note on why Cancel amend waits on the URL (don't care); and the animals backend unit tests that build a real DocumentService on stubbed repositories (keep, as they follow the house rule of not mocking the service's own modules).
Numbered item 5: the fixes land in as few increments as sensible, not one per item.

The heading of the closing block (line 22): these are the orchestrator's calls applying the ruling, which Sam accepted with "crack on" — so each bullet below is claimed as decided, with its lesser authority noted.

Applied call: the animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list (the health-certificate-owed list nothing reads), and the rule that works it out comes off the OutstandingItem enum; both are re-added with the future outstanding-actions banner. Claim that this replaces the 16 November ruling's "what stays: submitting records ... the outstanding items" (claim 2), naming that supersession, and that the submitted date is still recorded.
Applied call: "Answers differ from submitted" is a non-null yes/no flag.
Applied call: the animals frontend's local stub takes "answers changed" from the backend's shape (a stored flag, kept as the backend keeps it) rather than working it out itself.
Applied call: "Identification details" on the review gets a real GOV.UK heading class, not bold body text, in a sensible hierarchy under the species heading.
Applied call: review cards get their accessible names the way the rest of the service does.
Applied call: a missing notification on the review page shows the standard page not found, like every other page.
Applied call: the plants notification lifecycle spec gets the missing blank line before its first scenario.

Applied call: Delete on the header opens the delete confirmation page (a link, not a post), and applying item 2 it stays a link outside the Amend and Copy as new forms, so no action shares another's form.

Every claim quotes the ruling's own words and refs the file plus its numbered item or bullet, such as "ruling-sam-2026-11-19.md item 2" or "ruling-sam-2026-11-19.md applied call 1"; a listed point the quote says in so many words is verbatim, one it only implies is inferred with the implying words named.

Anything the ruling leaves open on a point it touches — for instance which increments item 5's "as few as sensible" groups the fixes into, or which review items item 4's "every other atypical item" covers, since the review itself is a separate source — is recorded as a gap claim with an empty quote, never as a decision.
